In the foreground, partially obscuring the lower right, are several smaller sharks or fish resting on the sand. The sturgeon displays characteristic bony scutes along its lateral line and dorsal ridge.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly elongated and tapered. While the mouth is not fully open to show protrusion, the ventral positioning of the snout structure is consistent with sturgeon anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, bony plates (scutes) are visible along the dorsal midline and the lateral line. The skin between them appears smooth, lacking typical fish scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is a dark grayish-brown, transitioning to a creamy white/lighter color on the belly, consistent with counter-shading.
The caudal fin is visible on the left; the upper lobe is significantly larger and more developed than the lower lobe, confirming the heterocercal structure.

The pectoral fin near the center appears somewhat melted into the body wall, lacking a sharp insertion point or clear ray structure, though this could be motion blur.
